elements.text: Investment case | Evidence and qualifications
Investment case: maintenance revenue and historical growth

Sources: company brief; management model (PnL, ServiceMix, CustomerSales); management interview; CFO email.
Full source locators and calculations are retained in slide notes.
NORTHBRIDGE  |  FICTIONAL TRAINING CASE  |  January 2026

rows: Scheduled maintenance: £17.5m, or 70% of FY2025 revenue. Contracts generally run for one to three years.
Renewal is by agreement. The 94% retention estimate has no defined cohort or calculation basis.
Revenue: £18.0m in FY2023 to £25.0m in FY2025; 17.9% CAGR. FY2025 EBITDA: £5.0m.
FY2025 revenue remains provisional versus £26.2m in the earlier brief. EBITDA is unaudited.
85 field engineers within 120 employees; hubs in Birmingham, Manchester and Bristol.
The founder leads major customer relationships. Relationship continuity requires diligence.
Add 20 net engineers by FY2027 and cross-sell maintenance to repair customers.
Execution depends on hiring and renewals. A customer-level forecast bridge is unavailable.

elements.text: Customer concentration
The top five customers represent 42% of FY2025 revenue; the largest represents 12%. Contract-level review is required.
Earnings evidence
No QoE report or EBITDA normalisation bridge has been supplied. Investment conclusions remain subject to financial diligence.

NORTHBRIDGE  |  FICTIONAL TRAINING CASE  |  January 2026
Founded in 2012, Northbridge provides scheduled maintenance, reactive repairs and installation work for industrial sites, logistics operations and facilities management.

rows: Ties to the provisional management model

elements.text: Delivery footprint

Three hubs: Birmingham, Manchester and Bristol.
85 field engineers within 120 employees at 31 December 2025. The founder leads major customer relationships.
Contract quality and revenue basis

Contracts generally run for one to three years, with renewal by agreement. Maintenance share does not establish revenue retention. FY2025 revenue remains provisional: £25.0m in the model versus £26.2m in the earlier brief.

elements.text: Financial analysis | Historical management actuals
Revenue reached a provisional £25.0m in FY2025

Sources: management model, PnL!B5:D11; earlier company brief; CFO email; management interview.
A = management actuals. Figures are unaudited; FY2025 revenue remains provisional.
NORTHBRIDGE  |  FICTIONAL TRAINING CASE  |  January 2026
GBP million unless stated. Year ending 31 December.
Historical development

Revenue increased from £18.0m to £25.0m between FY2023 and FY2025 (17.9% CAGR).

Management EBITDA rose from £2.7m to £5.0m. Reported margins were 15.0%, 18.1% and 20.0% across the three years.
Diligence focus

The earnings basis is management-reported. QoE, normalisation, debt, cash and working-capital schedules are unavailable. The revenue difference requires reconciliation before relying on the growth trend.
Revenue reconciliation remains open: £25.0m management model versus £26.2m earlier company brief. The CFO supports provisional use of the model; this does not resolve the difference.
